title: What an economic indicator is
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:46Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point's opening definition matches, but it also teaches the leading, coincident and lagging grouping, which is broader than the new point's plain definition of what an indicator is, so a new point fits better.

draft.title: Economic indicators
card: An economic indicator is a statistic that shows how the economy is going. It turns a big, messy picture into a number that can be tracked.
Common indicators include the growth rate, the unemployment rate and the inflation rate.
Each indicator measures one part of the economy. One number alone does not describe the whole economy.
Governments, businesses and households read indicators when they make decisions, such as setting a budget or deciding whether to hire.
draft.remember: An indicator is a statistic that measures one part of how the economy is going.

a.q: Which of these is an economic indicator?
opts: A new law on school uniforms
The score of a footy grand final
a.why: The unemployment rate is a statistic that shows how part of the economy is going. The other options are not statistics that measure how the economy is performing, so they are not indicators.
a.clue: Look for a statistic that measures the economy.

b.q: Priya reads that her state's unemployment rate fell this year. She says the economy is doing well in every way. What is wrong with her claim?
opts: One indicator measures only one part of the economy
Unemployment is not an economic indicator
A falling rate always means prices are also falling
Indicators only count for the whole country, not a state
b.why: Each indicator measures one part of the economy, so one number cannot show everything. Unemployment is an indicator, so the claim is not wrong for that reason. The fall tells us about jobs, not about prices.
b.clue: Think about what one number can cover.

b.best: One indicator measures only one part of the economy
